findings.statement: chunk verification pays on a skewed scan workload
findings.detail: Zipfian scans at 55285646 entries/s per chunk against 47589779 per block (chunk vs whole: greater 1.162x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 4.5%/5.7%)). This is the regime chunking can help in at all: a uniform sweep reaches every chunk of every block it touches, and verifying all of a block's chunks is verifying the block

findings.statement: verifying a chunk instead of a block makes a cold scan cheaper
findings.detail: cold scans at 39663014 entries/s per chunk against 40341188 per block (chunk vs whole: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.983, p=0.3067) -- within noise, not a result)

findings.statement: the first pass now costs about what the steady state does
findings.detail: per chunk: 39663014 entries/s cold against 57182771 warm (1.44x). Per block: 40341188 against 59429467 (1.47x). f19-coldscan measured the whole-block ratio at 1.65x, and closing it is the point of this change -- a scan that has to warm up is a scan whose first pass is charged for every block it will ever touch

notes: one file, two readers, interleaved; the only difference is ReadOptions::chunk_verify
